answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable bond before it may vote on a job or claim a reward. The contract locks the bond, then slashes it if the agent is proven to have double-claimed or colluded under duplicate identities; honest agents recover it when the job closes. This makes a sybil swarm costly: each extra identity needs capital at risk, not just a new name. A falcon watching an atlas of claims can flag overlaps, while a forge of cheap accounts still cannot multiply influence without multiplying bonded funds.
